cefrAlignment: Matches B1 (CEFR CV reading for information: can identify the main conclusions and significant points in straightforward newspaper articles on familiar subjects): 204–211-word local news reports. Headline grammar and reporting verbs are taught at an accessible level.
examFidelity: The articles and main-idea, detail and purpose questions fit TOEIC Part 7. The short answers follow the IELTS 'NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER' format, and every key fits the limit. The tips are consistent with exams.ts.
fixes: ex2: the keys for q1–q5 were all in position B; I moved the correct option in q2, q3, q5 and q6 so the positions vary
ex4 q5: moved the correct option from A to D (four of five keys were A)
ex3: added accepted answers for the snow depth ('over 40 centimeters', '40cm', etc.) and the flight count ('120 flights', 'around 120 flights')
learnerOutcome: A learner can decode headline grammar, find who, what, when, where and why in the lead, separate the main point from quotes and details, and choose a suitable headline.
